'''John Edwin Luecke''' is an American [[mathematician]] who works in [[topology]] and [[knot theory]].  He got his Ph.D. in 1985 from the [[University of Texas at Austin]] and is now a professor in the department of mathematics at that institution.

==Work==
Luecke specializes in  knot theory and [[3-manifold]]s. In a 1987 paper<ref>M. Culler, C. Gordon, J. Luecke, P. Shalen (1987). Dehn surgery on knots. The Annals of Mathematics (''Annals of Mathematics'') 125 '''(2)''': 237-300.</ref> Luecke, [[Marc Culler]], [[Cameron Gordon (mathematician)|Cameron Gordon]], and [[Peter Shalen]] proved the [[cyclic surgery theorem]].  In a 1989 paper<ref>Cameron Gordon and John Luecke, ''Knots are determined by their complements''.  [[Journal of the American Mathematical Society|J. Amer. Math. Soc.]] 2 (1989), no. 2, 371–415.</ref> Luecke and Cameron Gordon proved that knots are determined by their complements, a result now known as the [[Gordon–Luecke theorem]].

Dr Luecke received a [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] [[Presidential Young Investigator Award]]<ref>[http://www.utexas.edu/opa/experts/profile.php?id=255 The University of Texas at Austin; Faculty profile] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927075430/http://www.utexas.edu/opa/experts/profile.php?id=255 |date=2011-09-27 }}</ref><ref>[https://www.nsf.gov/awards/presidential.jsp NSF Presidential and Honorary Awards]</ref> in 1992 and [[Sloan Foundation]] fellow<ref>{{cite web|url=https://research.utexas.edu/honors-recognition/sloan-research-fellowships/|title=Sloan Research Fellowships|publisher=University of Texas at Austin|access-date=2024-03-03}}</ref> in 1994. In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-02-02.</ref>
